title: Elementary chains: unions that preserve first-order truth
summary: Take unions of elementary chains without changing first-order truth at old parameters, and distinguish this from one-way preservation in substructures.
abstract: Suppose we repeatedly enlarge a nonempty structure, preserving every first-order statement about the elements already present. Does taking the union preserve those statements too? Tarski's elementary chain theorem says yes: every stage remains an elementary submodel of the union. The crucial point is that a formula uses only finitely many parameters, and a witness in the union appears at some stage. Merely making all stages isomorphic does not suffice: the integer tails each have a least element, while their union does not. Universal and existential formulas also give useful one-way preservation rules for ordinary substructures.
